concepts.heading: Understanding Relationship Grief
concepts.alt: Gently holding a wilting flower, a single tear on her cheek
concepts.plain: Grief is not only for death. Breakups and changes bring it too.

concepts.heading: Why Relationship Grief Is Unique
concepts.alt: A guide looking at a framed photo while a faint outline of a person walks away in the distance
concepts.plain: It is harder because the person is still out there.

concepts.heading: Types of Relationship Grief
concepts.alt: A guide holding an umbrella while raindrops of different sizes fall
concepts.plain: There are several kinds, like grieving before the end has even come.

concepts.heading: The Grief Process
concepts.alt: A guide walking a winding path past five small blank signposts
concepts.plain: Grief moves through many feelings, and not in neat steps.

checks.explanation: Not reserved for death. Grief is not reserved for death. The end of a relationship — or even a significant change within one — can trigger a grief process as intense and valid as mourning a loved one who has died.

options: Mourning a relationship before it officially ends
checks.explanation: Mourning a relationship before it officially ends. Anticipatory grief: Mourning a relationship before it officially ends.

a7a07cfb-a155-46fd-994f-c28fca1ead8f.takeaway: Losing a relationship is real grief, even when the person is still alive.

concepts.heading: The Art of Conscious Uncoupling
concepts.alt: Calmly untying a ribbon that joined their wrists
concepts.plain: A breakup does not have to be a war. You can end things with care.

concepts.heading: What Conscious Uncoupling Is (and Isn't)
concepts.alt: Two guides shaking hands warmly with a small respectful nod
concepts.plain: It means ending on purpose and keeping your dignity, for both of you.

concepts.heading: The Five Steps
concepts.alt: A guide climbing five steps, each marked with a small heart
concepts.plain: There are five steps. The first is letting yourself feel it all without lashing out.

concepts.heading: Conscious Uncoupling in Different Situations
concepts.plain: Endings ripple outward to friends, family and other partners. Tell people with care.

concepts.heading: Practical Tools
concepts.alt: A guide writing a letter at a desk beside a candle
concepts.plain: Try a goodbye letter you never have to send. Start with what you are grateful for.

options: A deliberate way of ending a relationship while preserving dignity
checks.explanation: A deliberate way of ending a relationship while preserving dignity. It is a deliberate process of ending a romantic relationship while preserving dignity.

checks.prompt: What is the first of the five steps?
checks.explanation: Find emotional freedom. Step one is to find emotional freedom: let yourself fully feel without acting destructively on those feelings.

37040837-6f32-4c66-926d-25582dcd0b79.takeaway: You can end a relationship with care and respect, honouring what it gave you.

concepts.heading: Grief That Other People Don't See
concepts.alt: A guide sitting quietly beside a small candle
concepts.plain: Some losses go unseen by others. They are still real.

concepts.heading: Losses That Come With Having More Than One Partner
concepts.alt: A guide looking at one empty chair at a table set for four
concepts.plain: You can grieve when a partner's other relationship ends, because you lose something too.

concepts.heading: Why This Grief Is Often Invisible
concepts.alt: A guide holding an outlined see-through heart, looking unseen
concepts.plain: People say "but you still have other partners". That does not cancel the loss.

concepts.heading: Processing Grief Across Multiple Relationships
concepts.alt: A guide holding an umbrella with rain on one side and sunshine on the other
concepts.plain: It is hard to grieve one relationship while showing up for others. Be honest about it.

concepts.heading: Supporting a Grieving Partner
concepts.alt: D offering C a cup of tea and simply listening
concepts.plain: Do not compare or cheer them up. Just be there.

concepts.heading: Creating Grief Rituals
concepts.alt: A guide lighting a small candle beside a keepsake box
concepts.plain: Make your own goodbye rituals, since the usual ones do not fit.

checks.after: Why This Grief Is Often Invisible
checks.prompt: Why does grief often go unseen when someone has more than one partner?
options: Others dismiss it because you have other partners
checks.explanation: Others dismiss it because you have other partners. External invalidation is one reason: people dismiss the loss because you have other partners.

checks.prompt: How should you support a grieving partner?
options: Don't compare their grief to how you would feel
checks.explanation: Don't compare their grief to how you would feel. Don't compare their grief to how you'd feel, and don't suggest they should be over it.

8df70c07-e719-4677-bad9-aded9262696e.takeaway: Grief in open relationships is real even when other partners remain. Name it and make room for it.

concepts.heading: Transitions & Post-Relationship Growth
concepts.alt: Two guides exchanging a friendly fist bump, a single rose resting on a table beside them
concepts.plain: Some relationships change shape instead of ending.

concepts.heading: Relationship Transitions That Aren't Endings
concepts.alt: Each holding one handle of a pram, walking in step as a team
concepts.plain: Partners can become friends, co-parents or something else that fits better.

concepts.heading: The Transition Conversation
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting at a table with two cups, talking honestly and calmly
concepts.plain: A good transition talk is honest, kind and clear about what changes.

concepts.heading: Maintaining Connection Post-Transition
concepts.alt: A guide drawing a friendly dotted chalk line on the ground
concepts.plain: Clear limits on contact, touch and topics help you stay in each other's lives.

concepts.heading: Post-Traumatic Growth in Relationships
concepts.alt: A guide standing tall beside a green sprout growing from a cracked pot
concepts.plain: People often grow after hard endings.

concepts.heading: The Post-Relationship Growth Process
concepts.alt: A guide climbing wide steps toward a sunrise
concepts.plain: Recovery comes in phases. The first is steadying yourself with sleep, food, movement and friends.

checks.prompt: Which is a relationship transition that isn't an ending?
checks.explanation: Romantic to platonic. Romantic to platonic means choosing friendship over romance.

options: Growing in positive ways after a hard experience
checks.explanation: Growing in positive ways after a hard experience. Psychologists Tedeschi and Calhoun identified five domains in which people can grow after hardship.

e09dd82c-ed4b-4b44-a200-96d2e6f84463.takeaway: A relationship can change shape instead of ending, and hard endings can lead to growth.
